hypothesis: Each destination thread currently rereads source-particle fields from global memory throughout its serial scan. Cooperatively loading each 256-particle source tile once per block and reusing it across destination threads should reduce repeated global loads while preserving ascending source order and the existing force arithmetic.
notes: The existing 256-thread / 256-items-per-block configuration is retained as a compatible one-thread-per-output mapping; the static shared tile uses 4 KiB, so shared_memory_bytes remains 0. No candidate measurement or correctness result is available here. The controller should run the full correctness suite and measure all official sizes before retaining this candidate. The supplied baseline-e1 is valid and correct (11 cases; three-repeat mean 0.0018545204 s).
transformations: Added a thread-per-output kernel that cooperatively stages up to 256 source particles per tile in shared memory and reuses the tile across destination threads.
Kept all threads participating in tile barriers, including output-tail threads; source tails use a bounded tile count and self-interactions are skipped.
Retained the compatible 256/256 launch settings and unchanged serial accumulation order; made no extra launches or host-side changes.
